Transformer class = Embeddings (ResNetV2 CNN + 1x1 patch projection + position embeddings) followed by Encoder (12 Transformer layers + final LayerNorm); returns encoded tokens, attention weights and the list of CNN skip features

ResNetV2 (ResNet-50-style, block_units (3, 4, 9), width 64, weight-standardised convs + GroupNorm); built only when config.patches.grid is set (hybrid); returns the H/16 feature (C=1024) and three skip features [H/8 C=512, H/4 C=256, H/2 C=64]

stem: 7x7 stride-2 StdConv2d 3->64, GroupNorm(32), ReLU -> C=64, H/2xW/2; this pre-pooling output is appended as the H/2 skip feature (features[2] after reversal); the max-pool is applied afterwards in forward (the pool entry in the Sequential is commented out)

3 bottleneck units (PreActBottleneck), 64->256 channels, stride 1 -> C=256, H/4xW/4 (zero-padded to exactly H/4 when the unpadded max-pool leaves it one pixel short); output is the H/4 skip feature (features[1])
4 bottleneck units, 256->512 channels, first unit stride 2 -> C=512, H/8xW/8; output is the H/8 skip feature (features[0])
9 bottleneck units, 512->1024 channels, first unit stride 2 -> C=1024, H/16xW/16; this is the CNN feature map handed to patch embedding (not a skip)
Conv2d 1024->768 with kernel = stride = patch_size (1x1 in the hybrid model when the token grid equals the H/16 CNN map): the trainable linear projection E applied to every 1x1 patch
flattens the projected map (B, 768, h, w) into a token sequence (B, n_patches, 768); in code it runs after the projection conv
adds the learned position embeddings (nn.Parameter of shape (1, n_patches, 768); E_pos of the draft's Eq. 1), then dropout 0.1 -> z_0

Encoder = 12 x Block (class Block, line 168, same class at every layer), each pre-norm: LN -> MSA (12 heads x 64, softmax(QK^T/sqrt(64))V, output Linear) -> +residual; LN -> MLP (768->3072, GELU, ->768, dropout 0.1) -> +residual; then a final LayerNorm (encoder_norm) -> z_L (B, n_patches, 768)

DecoderCup: reshape tokens to a 2-D map, conv_more (768->512), then 4 cascaded upsampling blocks H/16 -> H/8 -> H/4 -> H/2 -> H with decoder channels 256, 128, 64, 16; the first n_skip=3 blocks concatenate a CNN skip feature
(B, n_patch, 768) -> permute -> (B, 768, h, w) with h = w = int(sqrt(n_patch)), i.e. H/16xW/16; done inside DecoderCup.forward

unclear: REPO holds only networks/ (vit_seg_configs.py, vit_seg_modeling.py, vit_seg_modeling_resnet_skip.py). The script that builds the model and sets img_size, n_classes, n_skip or patches.grid is not in REPO, so all values here are the defaults of get_r50_b16_config; n_classes = 2 in particular is a config default, not necessarily the dataset's class count.

Patch size vs image size: patch_size = img_size // 16 // grid. With the config's grid (16, 16) this gives 1x1 patches only at img_size 256, and (0, 0) at VisionTransformer's default img_size 224, so a caller outside REPO must set grid = img_size/16. The decoder also assumes 1x1 patches: up_block_1 upsamples the sqrt(n_patches) token grid x2 and concatenates it with the H/8 CNN feature, which only matches when the token grid is H/16. So the encoded feature is H/16 x W/16 (effective P = 16) with 1x1 patches, which agrees with the draft's 1x1-patch statement.

Order of tokenisation: the code projects first (Conv2d with kernel = stride = patch size) and then flattens/transposes into a sequence. The draft orders it sequentialise-then-project. For 1x1 patches the two are equivalent; the ids seq and patch_embed follow the code order.
The reshape of z_L is done inside DecoderCup.forward, so reshape has parent cup; the draft recorded it as top-level.

Upsampling block, code vs draft text: the code runs bilinear x2 upsample, then concatenation with the skip, then TWO Conv2dReLU (3x3 conv + BatchNorm + ReLU). The draft text describes one 3x3 conv + ReLU. Two parts are not in the draft: an extra conv_more (3x3 conv 768->512 + BN + ReLU) before the first block, and a SegmentationHead (3x3 conv 16->n_classes, no upsampling) after the last block.

Skip merge is channel concatenation (torch.cat, dim=1) after upsampling and before the convs, not addition. In the default config (n_skip = 3) three skips feed up_blocks 1-3: ResNet block2 (C=512, H/8), block1 (C=256, H/4) and the stem (C=64, H/2, taken before max-pool). up_block_4 (H/2 -> H) has no skip, and config.skip_channels[3] = 16 is zeroed by the n_skip re-selection. The skip edges keep kind 'skip' even though they depend on the count n_skip; their labels start 'if n_skip >= k:'.

The main decoder path is drawn entering each block at its concat_k (the first inner component recorded); the x2 upsample that comes before it and the two convs after it are collapsed into up_block_k. The block's output edge leaves from up_block_k.

The CNN stage components (cnn_root, cnn_block1-3) go one level deeper than the overview depth rule requires inside a reused CNN. They are kept because the three skips tap different stages; collapse them into cnn if the figure draws the CNN as one box.
The Transformer layer's internals (LN, MSA, MLP, residual adds) are collapsed into transformer because it is a reused block. Its z_L includes a final LayerNorm (encoder_norm) after the 12th layer.

Non-hybrid configs (no patches.grid, e.g. ViT-B_16): the raw image is patch-embedded with 16x16 patches and features = None, so the decoder runs without skips. This path is recorded only as the 'if not hybrid:' edge.

Spatial sizes H/2, H/4, H/8, H/16 assume a square input with H divisible by 16. ResNetV2.forward pads to (right_size, right_size) from the height alone, and DecoderCup takes h = w = int(sqrt(n_patch)). The unpadded 3x3/2 max-pool leaves the H/4 map one pixel short, and the code zero-pads it at the bottom and right.

The model returns logits only. config.activation = 'softmax' is set but never read in REPO, CrossEntropyLoss is imported but unused, and no loss is defined in REPO. VisionTransformer's num_classes (default 21843) and zero_head arguments are stored but unused; the head width comes from config['n_classes'].
PreActBottleneck, despite its name, applies conv -> GroupNorm -> ReLU in each step, with a ReLU after the residual add. It is a detail inside the reused CNN and is left out of the components.
